scenes.tts: Does a probe with nine hundred sixty recording sites record nine hundred sixty neurons? No. The original Neuropixels probe had that many sites on one shank. But it could address only three hundred eighty four at a time. Two probes in an awake mouse recorded more than seven hundred well isolated neurons at once, from five brain structures.

scenes.tts: Neurons are not read off sites. Spike sorting software groups spikes into units, using the shape of each spike and the sites where it appears. One neuron shows up on several neighbouring sites, and one site hears several neurons. So a unit can merge two neurons, or split one. Treat each unit as an inference, with quality scores, not a confirmed single neuron.
scenes.visual: A column of sites with neurons beside it: one neuron lights three sites, two neurons share one site; a unit box merges two neurons, and one neuron gets two unit chips.

scenes.tts: Now count what you have, in an invented dataset. Two mice, A and B, each have two sessions. Each unit appears in one session only. Six units, each watched for four trials, make twenty four unit trials. But units in one mouse share its conditions, so they are not independent observations.

scenes.tts: Each unit gets a rate in spikes per second: eight, two, four, eight, two and two. Pooled, the rate is four point three three spikes per second. But mouse A supplied twice the units of mouse B. Weight each mouse equally, and mouse A averages five point five while mouse B averages two. The animal mean is three point seven five spikes per second.
scenes.caption: Each unit gets a rate in spikes per second: 8, 2, 4, 8, 2 and 2. Pooled, the rate is 4.33 spikes per second. But mouse A supplied twice the units of mouse B. Weight each mouse equally, and mouse A averages 5.5 while mouse B averages 2. The animal mean is 3.75 spikes per second.
scenes.visual: The six units show their rates; a pooled value 4.33 in red; mouse brackets turn to mouse means 5.5 and 2; the animal mean 3.75 in green.

scenes.tts: Count every unit trial as an independent sample, and n is twenty four. That mistake has a name, pseudoreplication. For a claim about mice, n is two, not twenty four. Many units from one mouse are still one mouse, and the sample size belongs to the level of the question.

scenes.tts: Each number here measures something other than what you might assume. Sites are not channels, and channels are not neurons. A unit is an inference, and one animal can supply many units. Report the whole hierarchy: animals, sessions, units and trials. Then say which level your question is about.
